text:
Tristan Jarry needed only 18 saves to post the shutout, but the night was less lopsided than 4-0 suggests. The Edmonton goalie was drafted 44th overall by the Penguins in 2013, out of Edmonton, and he stood in his hometown's colors at UBS Arena and gave the Islanders nothing. By our numbers he saved 2.1 goals more than the shots he faced deserved, meaning the Islanders' chances were good enough to score about twice and Jarry stopped every one.

The game turned in the second period. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins scored at 8:42 and Vasily Podkolzin followed 68 seconds later, then Nugent-Hopkins added a power-play goal at 18:26 to make it 3-0. Jason Dickinson finished it late in the third on a shot with only a 5% chance of going in. Nugent-Hopkins, the No. 1 pick in 2011, was the first star with two goals and the best individual numbers on the ice.

Yet the quality of chances was close. Edmonton's expected goals (the measure of how good each shot was) came to 2.3 against 2.14 for New York, and our simulation of every shot gives Edmonton just 52% to win. The Islanders had the better of the third period, 1.02 to 0.68, and Victor Eklund's 21% look was turned away by Jarry. Ilya Sorokin allowed three goals on 2.25 expected, so he was a little worse than average, and the rest was finishing and a goalie who never blinked. We have no records or streaks to add for either club.
